penetration_assumption: The Rs 85,000 is the ASSORTMENT-ONLY gap and it is small on purpose. Built bottom-up from ARY's own observed per-SKU performance, not from a national benchmark. VERIFIED anchor: the 78 hot-beverage SKUs that actually sold in the live 12m window (excluding the 2 institutional loose-tea SKUs) did Rs 4.91 L — mean Rs 6,295/SKU/yr, MEDIAN Rs 3,014/SKU/yr. I size at the median, not the mean, because the mean is carried by a single Rs 10 Nescafe 3.2g sachet doing 7,779 units. (a) GENUINELY ABSENT, 6 defensible new lines: 4 at median Rs 3,014 (Kangra 250g x2, badam/kesar milk-masala powder, Ensure Diabetes Care) + 2 at 3x median Rs 9,042 (Protinex/Ensure adult nutrition — the only absent MUST-HAVE, and it has a named on-campus buyer: Akal Hospital Rs 78,210/yr and Akal De-Addiction Ward Rs 2.31 L/yr already buy from ARY) = Rs 30,100. (b) LISTED-BUT-DORMANT, 17 distinct lines worth re-stocking (Nescafe/Bru Gold freeze-dried, Pediasure + Junior Horlicks, 3-in-1 tea/coffee premix incl. 1kg vending packs, chai-masala powder, kadha/kwath + kahwa, caffeine-free herbal, Amul whitener, bulk SMP): ARY's base rate is 27.8% of listed hot-bev SKUs selling at all; assume deliberate selection lifts that to 50%, so 8.5 lines work at the median = Rs 25,600 (Rs 53,500 if they hit the mean). Central estimate Rs 55,000; range Rs 70,000–1,50,000 across the median/mean band; I report Rs 85,000. Gross margin Rs 14,000 uses the VERIFIED 16.47% realised margin (below). THE NUMBER THAT MATTERS IS NOT THIS ONE: keeping the 78 SKUs that ALREADY sell in stock for 12 months instead of 6.3 is worth +Rs 2,39,665/yr (+49%) and Rs 39,470 of gross profit — 3x the entire assortment gap, with zero new SKUs. Assumption there: each SKU sells at its observed in-stock monthly rate for all 12 months, capped at 2x its actual to stop absurd extrapolation.
probe_evidence:
DB live to 2026-08-30 20:46; window 2025-09-01 to 2026-08-31. ARY net Rs 7.50 Cr (gross Rs 7.67 Cr − returns Rs 17.09 L), 372,352 bills — all VERIFIED.

CATEGORY SIZE (VERIFIED, direct group/subgroup SQL, not name-match): Tea & Coffee group 239 active SKUs / 66 selling / Rs 5,80,673. Malt-HFD subgroups (Health Drink, Horlicks, Complan, Chocolate Powder) 56 / 14 / Rs 68,185. Whitener+condensed 14 / 6 / Rs 44,214. TOTAL packaged Rs 6,93,072 = 0.92% of net sales, on 309 listed SKUs of which 86 sell (27.8%).

THE 22.8% THAT ISN'T RETAIL: Rs 1,57,858 of that is ONE customer. "Tea 1Kg" (Rs 91,858) and "Tea_L" (Rs 66,000) — the #1 and #3 SKUs in the whole category — were bought 100% by "Hunger Heroes", 12 invoices, 60 kg each, 720 kg total. That is the langar/mess supply account (ARY's largest customer at Rs 70.6 L/yr across rice, atta, vegetables, pulses). I nearly filed "Tea 1Kg out of stock since 11 May" as an availability finding; the customer query killed it — they order 60 kg when they need it. Retail packaged hot beverages = Rs 5,35,214 = Rs 114/resident/yr = Rs 9.50/resident/month.

MARGIN (VERIFIED from PurchaseDetail.ItemValue/Quantity vs realised SaleDetail rate, 12m, not the price master): retail packaged 16.47% (69 SKUs, Rs 4.65 L rev, Rs 76,555 GP); institutional loose tea 9.47%. Excluded 2 SKUs with corrupt cost rows (Red Label 22 Gm: cost Rs 206 vs sale Rs 17.33 — carton/unit mismatch; Tata Tea Gold 19 Gm: cost Rs 0.001). This is HIGHER than the demand research assumed (it guessed 5-9% on economy CTC; ARY realises 13-17% on branded tea).

METHOD TRAP I HIT AND FIXED — report this upstream: in zsh, `./ary assort probe $terms` does NOT word-split, so a multi-word variable is passed as ONE substring term and returns 0 matches. My first pass "found" kangra, kahwa, kadha and tea-masala all absent this way. Every verdict below was re-run with separately quoted args. That failure mode is invisible — it returns a clean, well-formatted zero.

RE-PROBED WITH MULTIPLE WORD VARIANTS (all separately quoted):
• GENUINELY ABSENT (0 SKUs anywhere in the catalogue): Kangra/HP GI tea (probe kangra palampur dharamshala "wah tea" "himachal tea" → 0). South-Indian filter/chicory coffee (probe "filter coffee" chicory levista cothas "green label" malgudi narasus → 0; a looser probe returns only water filters and kitchen utilities). Decaf (probe decaf decaffeinated → 0). Adult/elderly clinical nutrition (probe protinex ensure fresubin nutrilite → 0 — the ONLY absent must-have). Diabetic nutrition (probe diabetes diabetic "sugar control" → 0). Maternity/lactation (0). Badam/kesar milk-masala POWDER (probe "milk masala" thandai "badam mix" → 2 SKUs, both RTD flavoured milk, both dormant). Whey/plant protein (0). Millet/ragi/sattu drink (matches are atta, biscuits, cornflakes — no drink).
• FALSE ABSENT, caught by variant spelling: Pediasure is LISTED — 6 SKUs filed as "Abbott Pedia Sure" (space), all in Food Supplement > Horlicks, all zero sales. A `%pediasure%` search misses every one.
• FALSE COVERED in the supplied diff: it credits "Tea masala / chai masala spice powder" as covered with Rs 16,330 on a `tea + masala` AND-match. Live check: that Rs 16,330 is Brooke Bond Taaza MASALA CHAI tea (Rs 10,530 + Rs 5,820). The actual chai-masala spice powders — Ruchi Tea Masala 20 Gm (Spices > Masala) and Keya Chai Masala 90 Gm (filed under Salt & Sugar > SALT) — did Rs 0 in 12 months. Line is DORMANT, not covered.
• The diff's broad matches are unusable in the covered direction: it credits single lines with Rs 30.4 L on 'blue', Rs 34.9 L on 'white', Rs 12.6 L on 'cadbury', Rs 18.4 L on 'amul', Rs 5.5 L on 'green', Rs 2.4 L on 'original'. ARY's ENTIRE hot-beverage vocabulary is Rs 6.93 L. Any line the diff credited above that figure was matching soap, chocolate, noodles or vegetables. 33 of its 54 lines rest on such a match; coveragePct 36.6 / commodityOnlyPct 61.0 should both be discarded.

CLASSIFICATION OF ALL 54 RESEARCHED LINES: 25 covered (a working substitute sells) / 20 listed-but-dormant / 9 genuinely absent. Zero must-have lines are absent except adult clinical nutrition, which is a pharmacy line, not a hot beverage.

THE AVAILABILITY EVIDENCE (this is the finding): of the 42 tea/coffee SKUs doing >Rs 2,000, only 4 sold in all 12 months and 21 have ZERO on-hand right now — Nescafe Classic 3.6g (Rs 19,240, sold 3/12 months, 0 stock), Nescafe Classic 45g (Rs 16,945, 6/12), Jivo Premium Tea 250g (Rs 11,040, 6/12), Bournvita 81g pouch (Rs 10,590, 5/12), Bru 6g (Rs 11,390, 7/12), Taaza 75g (Rs 8,800, 8/12, 0 stock). Monthly SKU count sold never exceeds 34 of 239 listed. Category shape is textbook over-listed / under-stocked, exactly the corpus-level finding.

SEASONALITY CORRECTION for the demand research: it assumed "+30-50% Oct-Mar hill winter". VERIFIED monthly series says the opposite — Jan (Rs 15,275 tea) and Feb (Rs 14,965) are the WEAKEST months, Sep-Oct and May-Jun the strongest. Demand tracks the academic calendar, not the weather. Buying deep for a hill winter would strand capital in the emptiest months.

blockers: THE BINDING CONSTRAINT IS REORDER DISCIPLINE, NOT SHELF SPACE. 21 of the 42 tea/coffee SKUs doing >Rs 2,000 are at zero on-hand today; only 4 of 42 sold in all 12 months. Adding 6 SKUs to a range where 173 of 239 already never sell makes the reorder problem worse, not better. De-list before you add.

MASTER-DATA POLLUTION. The dormant tail is largely duplicate master rows, not stocking decisions: 12 separate Red Label rows, 'Nescafe Nescafe Classic Coffee 25 Gm 3841' and '...3844', 'Brooke Bond Red Label Tea 250 Gm 3849', 8 identical 'Holy Leaf Green Tea 100 Gm' rows numbered 1/4/6/8/10/11/16. Any re-stock plan must dedupe first or it will buy the same thing four times.

UNVERIFIED AND DECISIVE — FREE LANGAR TEA. Baru Sahib is a Kalgidhar Trust campus with a community kitchen. The data is consistent with tea being served free: the paid counter sold 4,237 cups of tea in 12 months (11.6/day for 4,700 people) while paid Cold Coffee did Rs 2,18,850 and Espresso Rs 1,46,220 — residents pay for coffee, not chai. If langar tea is free and universal, retail tea demand is structurally capped and NO assortment change moves it. This cannot be answered from FusionERP8. Ask the operator before any tea buy.

SUPPLIER REACH FROM RAJGARH, SIRMAUR HP. One truck a week. The Palampur Kangra co-op and the D2C roasters the research names (Blue Tokai, Sleepy Owl, Bevzilla) have no distributor into Sirmaur; direct-to-store MOQs would tie up capital against a line I size at Rs 3,000/yr. Kangra is only worth it if it is bought as gift hampers for Trust visitors and donors, which is a merchandising decision, not a shelf SKU.

NO LICENCE OR COLD-CHAIN BLOCKER EXISTS HERE. Every line in scope is ambient and already inside ARY's FSSAI scope. The constraint is working capital and shelf turns only — which is why the honest answer is stocking discipline, not range.

OUT OF SCOPE BUT LARGER THAN THE WHOLE ASSORTMENT GAP: the manned counter. Rs 4,29,495 across 26 counter SKUs of which only 4 sell, at Ary G Canteen and Ary Lite. Tea Cup at 11.6 cups/day is the single most under-performing thing I found in this category. That is a service and staffing question and I have not sized it.
kill_reason: Not a kill, but the ADD-A-SKU framing is dead and the proof is arithmetic. ARY lists 309 hot-beverage SKUs and sells 86 of them (27.8%). The whole packaged category is Rs 6.93 L = 0.92% of a Rs 7.50 Cr business, and 22.8% of that is one institutional customer buying loose tea 60 kg at a time. Of the 54 lines the blind research says a store here should carry, 25 are covered, 20 are already listed and dead, and 9 are genuinely absent — and of those 9, exactly one is a must-have (Protinex/Ensure adult nutrition, which is a pharmacy line). The research fleet's raw recommendation for this category cannot be worth more than about Rs 85,000 a year, Rs 14,000 of gross profit, because the average hot-beverage SKU that WORKS at ARY earns Rs 3,014 a year and there is no listed line left that is both absent and wanted. Meanwhile the same 78 SKUs that already sell, kept in stock 12 months instead of an average of 6.3, are worth +Rs 2,39,665 and Rs 39,470 of gross profit for no new listings and no new suppliers. Spending a buyer's week on 6 new SKUs while Nescafe 3.6g, Nescafe 45g, Bru 6g and the Bournvita 81g pouch sit at zero stock is the exact mistake the corpus-level finding warned about.
